approach: Root cause: the scope guard learns why an attempt stopped from free-text closing-reason prefixes kept in two places that disagree (`scope_guard::ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` and `disk::is_environment_reason`, which lists only LOW_DISK and CHECK_TIMEOUT). A producer that dies on an expired login is closed as "the producer did not complete: success: ... API Error: 401 ...", which reads as a work failure, so it counts as line spend and attempts. The stored pause is never rechecked. Fix: (1) `disk.rs` gets one classifier `StopCause::of(reason)` and one parser `api_error_status(detail)` that recognises only the CLI's API-error form (401 = producer login expired, 429 = usage limit). No word lists. (2) `producer.rs` closes a producer stop through `disk::producer_stop_reason(detail)`, which uses the same parser. (3) `scope_guard.rs` drops its own prefix, adds a pure `verdict_of(JobState, Option<&str>)`, and `line_pause` recomputes the signals from the line's attempts and returns a stored pause only while the recomputed level is Pause. Revision: the recompute takes its p90 forecast from the newest request on the line that has a finished attempt, through one helper `line_forecast_p90` that `try_watch_line` also uses. That is the request whose reading was in force when the pause was written, so a new request joining the line (with no reading yet) cannot drop a T3 pause. Tests for the stored form build the detail through the real driver path (`StreamState::on_line` then `output_from_result`), not a hand-written string.

decisions.choice: One classifier `StopCause::of(&str)` in disk.rs. `is_environment_reason`, `resumable_stop` and the guard's `verdict_of` all call it. `ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX` leaves scope_guard.rs and lives only in disk.rs.
decisions.reason: The fault is two lists that disagree. With one definition a new environment kind is added once and both the guard and `athena retry` see it. disk.rs already owns the reason texts and `resumable_stop`.

rejected.option: Add the 401 text to `is_environment_reason` and keep the guard's own prefix check
rejected.why: Keeps two lists and fixes one instance.

rejected.option: Add a stored stop-reason field to a record such as the outcome
rejected.why: Needs a record schema and round-trip changes, and old records would lack it. The closing reason already carries the cause.

decisions.choice: Classify API errors only by the CLI's API-error form and HTTP status, in one `api_error_status(detail)` in disk.rs. The detail is `<subtype>: <first 300 chars of result text>` (`output_from_result`, claude.rs:249-281). Accept an optional subtype of exactly `success` or `error`, then an optional `Failed to authenticate. `, then require `API Error: ` followed by digits. 401 gives ProducerAuth, 429 gives UsageLimit. Words such as token, quota, rate limit, oauth or unauthorized are matched nowhere. The write path (`producer_stop_reason`) and the read path (`StopCause::of` on stored 'the producer did not complete: ' reasons) call the same function.
decisions.reason: A model's last words under `error_max_turns` or `error_during_execution` are free prose and can mention any of those words. Tying the class to the structured marker and its status makes a false positive need text that begins with 'API Error: 401' under subtype success or error. A false positive switches off T1/T3/T5 for that attempt, so the rule stays narrow. One parser keeps stored and new records on one rule. The `success` subtype with is_error set is what `output_from_result` produces for a CLI error result, since `ok` needs both `!is_error` and subtype `success`.

rejected.option: Match loose words like 'quota', 'rate limit', 'token' or 'unauthorized' anywhere in the detail
rejected.why: They are ordinary words in code work and model text; the 'the producer did not complete: ' prefix is on every producer failure, so it narrows nothing.

rejected.option: Add an API-error class field to AgentOutput and ResultEvent and pass it to producer_stop_reason
rejected.why: Better in principle, but AgentOutput is built in many places and fakes, and old stored records have no field, so a text rule is needed anyway. Left as a follow-up.

rejected.option: Accept 403, error type names such as authentication_error, or any 4xx
rejected.why: Not seen in the repository; each added form widens the false-positive surface.

decisions.choice: Keep the state gate. `verdict_of` and `resumable_stop` give Environment or resumable only for `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Failed)`, as `attempt_of` does today. `run/mod.rs` is not edited.
decisions.reason: The timed-out path (`keep_timed_out_work`) shares the 'the producer did not complete: ' prefix, so reason text alone cannot tell the cases apart; the state does. `settle_resume_marks` (mod.rs:594) already requires Failed plus `is_environment_reason` and picks up the new classifier unchanged.

rejected.why: A timed-out job whose text carried the API-error form would be excused from line spend.

decisions.choice: Compute the pause on read. `line_pause` recomputes the line's signals from its attempts under the current classification rule and returns the stored pause only while the recomputed overall level is Pause. The file is not deleted or edited. Recompute only invalidates a stored pause; it never creates one. Only `try_watch_line` writes a pause.
decisions.reason: Fixes stale pauses after a rule change with no migration; editing pause files is out of scope. Pauses for real repeated rejections still hold because the recomputed signals reach Pause again.

rejected.option: Delete the pause file when the signals clear
rejected.why: Out of scope and loses the record.

rejected.option: Store a rule version in the pause
rejected.why: Needs a new mark field and a version policy; recompute needs neither.

decisions.choice: Finding 1 answer. The recompute uses the p90 forecast in force when the pause was written: a single helper `line_forecast_p90(records, requests, line)` returns `forecast_p90_dollars` of the newest request in the line whose `attempts` is non-empty (a finished attempt), or 0.0 when none. `try_watch_line` and `line_pause` both call it. Only the attempt classification is re-evaluated under the current rule; the forecast is not re-derived from whichever request is newest. `t3_basis` still applies the VERIFIER_SHARE adjustment for a resumed last attempt, as at write time.
decisions.reason: The critic is right that the plan's earlier `line_state` read the forecast of the line's newest request. `line_pause` runs at reading.rs:1034 and run/mod.rs:704 for a request that has just joined the line and has no reading, so `forecast_p90_dollars` returned 0.0 and `t3_cost` (which pauses only when forecast > 0) dropped every T3 pause. A request with no finished attempt is skipped, so a joining request cannot change the forecast. At write time the just-attempted job is the newest request with a finished attempt, so write and read agree on the same records. The existing test `t3_pause_from_reading_forecast` already has the `go` call site (it asks `b`, a retry with no reading, and expects the T3 refusal); it must keep passing.

rejected.option: Use the newest request's forecast in both places (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Drops every T3 pause once a new request joins the line, as the finding shows.

That value is already scaled by t3_basis for a resumed attempt, so scaling it again would double the VERIFIER_SHARE factor, and hand-made marks carry 0.0. The raw p90 from the records is the exact write-time input.

rejected.option: Skip recompute for T3 pauses and trust the stored file
rejected.why: A T3 pause caused by environment-stop spend would then never clear; the attempt classification is the thing that changed.

decisions.choice: `live_marks` (used by status) rules: a Pause mark is shown only if the recomputed level is Pause. A Flag mark is shown while the recomputed level is Flag or Pause, with the stored kind. A mark for a line with no attempts in the records is shown unchanged. All use the same `line_forecast_p90`.
decisions.reason: A pause is written only by the guard after an attempt, so status never invents one; a mark with nothing to recompute from is the only evidence, and it keeps `status_lists_flagged_and_paused_lines` valid.

rejected.option: Hide a mark for a line with no attempts
Upgrade a stored flag to a pause in status
rejected.why: status must not write the guard's decisions.

decisions.choice: Split `attempt_of` so `verdict_of(state, reason)` is a pure function, and put the signal evaluation of `try_watch_line` into a private helper `line_state(records, requests, line)` that `line_pause` also calls. The helper takes the forecast from `line_forecast_p90` (finding 1).
decisions.reason: Tests drive real closing reasons through the production mapping without building JobRecords, and write and read paths cannot drift apart because they share both the attempt list and the forecast rule.

rejected.why: Heavy and brittle; the existing Rig covers the end-to-end path.

decisions.choice: Finding 2 answer. Stored-form tests build the detail through the real driver path: a JSON `result` line (`type` result, `subtype` success, `is_error` true, `result` 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 {... OAuth ... expired ...}') goes through `athena_agent::stream::StreamState::on_line`, then `athena_agent::claude::output_from_result`, and the `detail` is passed to `producer_stop_reason` and to `StopCause::of` on the legacy 'the producer did not complete: ' + detail form. A `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn driver_detail(result_json: &str) -> String` in disk.rs only wires those two production functions (no parsing of its own); scope_guard tests reuse it.
decisions.reason: The detail is built only by `output_from_result`, a pure function of a ResultEvent, and `parse_result` builds that from the CLI's JSON. Using both means the real formatter produces the input, so a mismatch in the 'subtype: text' shape fails the test. No fixture in crates/ contains 'API Error' or 'OAuth' (critic's Grep), so the JSON line itself is written from the brief; the parse path is real.

rejected.why: A drift in the real formatter would go unseen. One literal stays only as a control for the stored-record read path.
Skips `parse_result`, the code that sets is_error and subtype from the CLI JSON.

risks.risk: The API-error rule is too broad, so a real work failure is classed as environment and a runaway line is never paused.
risks.mitigation: Accept only subtype `success` or `error` (never `error_max_turns` or `error_during_execution`), require 'API Error: ' and a 401 or 429 status. Negative tests: model text under `error_max_turns` that mentions '401', 'token', 'rate limit', 'quota' or begins 'API Error: 401'; 'success: ' text with those words but no marker; 'API Error: 500'; a compile error containing 401; a verifier rejection.

risks.risk: The rule is too narrow and misses the real expired-login text, so the incident repeats.
risks.mitigation: Write and read paths share `api_error_status`, so new stops are classified as they are later read. Tests pass the JSON through the real parser and formatter. The open question names what to check.

risks.risk: Recompute changes which pauses hold: T3 pauses vanish if the forecast is read from the wrong request (finding 1).
risks.mitigation: `line_forecast_p90` takes the forecast of the newest request with a finished attempt, shared by write and read. Test 4 covers a real T3 pause with a new reading-less request, at the `go` and `retry` call sites. `t3_pause_from_reading_forecast` must keep passing.

risks.risk: Recompute breaks existing tests that write a hand-made pause for a line whose attempts do not reach Pause (for example `retry_refuses_paused_line`).
risks.mitigation: Change those tests to a real pause (script `[Some(0), Some(0)]`, as `t4_pause_via_go_and_ask` does). `status_lists_flagged_and_paused_lines` stays valid because its lines are unknown and keep their marks.

risks.risk: A producer stop on auth leaves no resume mark, so `athena retry` might be expected to resume a candidate that does not exist.
risks.mitigation: `resume_seed` with no mark starts from the base. Criterion 5 tests `resumable_stop`; a Rig test confirms the settle step spends no mark.

open_questions: The JSON of an expired-login result is taken from the brief ('401 OAuth access token has expired'), not from a stored record; no fixture in crates/ has 'API Error'. The test drives the real `parse_result` and `output_from_result`, but the CLI's exact JSON shape (is_error true, subtype success, 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ...') is an assumption. If a real sample shows another lead-in, `api_error_status` must accept it; the producer should note this if it finds one.
The usage-limit text is not in the repository. Only 'API Error: 429' is matched; a usage-limit stop in another form stays work until a sample is found.
A follow-up could pass the API-error class and status from the result event instead of re-parsing the detail; not done because AgentOutput and its fakes would change.
TimedOut producer stops (mod.rs `keep_timed_out_work`) still count as work in the guard. That is a different cause and is left as is.

`line_forecast_p90` skips requests without a finished attempt. If an owner lifts a pause and a later attempt finishes before the mark is rewritten, the forecast moves to that later request; the mark would be rewritten by that attempt's `try_watch_line` anyway.
